profile.commute: nine miles on the Burke-Gilman trail on a steel Surly

memories.text: Launched the skiff, which is called Puffin, at half five and the outboard needed nine pulls before it caught.
We run twelve eelgrass transects in Padilla Bay and transect seven is the only one that has gained shoot density two years running.
Decided to move the sampling window two hours earlier so we catch the minus one point four foot low tide instead of fighting the flood.
Sputnik learned to imitate the microwave finishing beep and now nobody in the house trusts the microwave.
The bell on my Surly cracked clean in half on the Fremont section of the trail and I rang it anyway for the rest of the ride out of habit.
Argued with my co-lead Priyanka about whether to keep the quadrat at half a metre or go to a quarter, and we agreed to run both on transect three.
My mate goes in a dented steel thermos with a strip of orange survey tape wrapped around the neck so it does not get mixed up with the sample bottles.
Spent the evening rewiring the trailer lights on my dad's boat trailer and got the left indicator working but not the right.
Counted forty-one Dungeness crab in the shallows on one pass, which is more than the whole of last August put together.
Decided to write the paper around the sediment result rather than the shoot counts, because the sediment story is the one that actually surprised us.
The GoPro flooded on the second drop because I did not seat the gasket, and I lost about forty minutes of underwater footage.
A tribal shellfish biologist named Owen showed me where the eelgrass edge used to sit in the nineties and it is about thirty metres out from where it is now.
Decided to swap the drone survey for a kayak transect on Thursday because the forecast has the wind at eighteen knots after two in the afternoon.
Waded out and found a purple sea star on the riprap, which is the first one I have seen at that site since 2023, and I sat down in the water for a minute.
The freezer in the lab has three hundred and sixty sample vials in it and exactly one of them has a label that has come off, which is now my problem.
Rode the Burke-Gilman in at twenty past six and got stuck behind a heron standing in the middle of the trail near Matthews Beach for a full minute.
Told Priyanka that the quarter metre quadrat gave us tighter numbers on transect three, so we are switching all twelve over from next week.
Sputnik will only take millet from my left hand, and if you offer it with the right hand he turns his back and sulks on the far perch.
